fields.before: This question asks which fact goes into which cell of a SWOT analysis matrix. The two axes of the figure are internal environment / external environment and favorable side / unfavorable side, so a = internal × favorable (Strength), b = internal × unfavorable (Weakness), c = external × favorable (Opportunity), and d = external × unfavorable (Threat). According to [situation of Company S], (1) is that the number of sales offices is smaller than that of other companies, and (2) is that competing Company T has decided to withdraw from the health snack business. The sales offices in (1) are a management resource that Company S owns itself and can increase or decrease at its own discretion, so they belong to the internal environment; having fewer of them than other companies is an unfavorable side for Company S, that is, a weakness, so (1) goes into b. The withdrawal of Company T in (2) is an event on the side of another company and the market that Company S cannot control, so it belongs to the external environment; with one fewer competitor, Company S can more easily expand its share, which is a tailwind, that is, a favorable side = an opportunity, so (2) goes into c. Therefore the combination is (1)=b and (2)=c, and the correct answer is ア.

Among the items in 〔S Company’s situation〕, the ones that count as strengths are (3) product planning ability higher than that of competitors, and (8) the fact that turning customers into members has gathered customer information and has also succeeded in acquiring wealthy members. The CRM (Customer Relationship Management) system in choice イ is a mechanism that analyzes the accumulated purchase data of customers and provides finely tailored, attentive service to each individual member, thereby deepening the relationship with customers. This is exactly a measure that uses an information system to further extend the existing strength in (8), that membership has gathered customer information, and it matches Policy Plan 1. The correct answer is therefore イ.

fields.before: The correct answer is イ. To copy files between two PCs over a wireless LAN, the two PCs must first join the same wireless network. The name that identifies a wireless LAN network is the ESSID (SSID), and PCs that connect to the same access point (or the same wireless network) must be given the same ESSID. In イ, both the current PC and the old PC have the ESSID A0B1C2D3E4, so they match and can join the same wireless LAN. Next, once they have joined the same network, they must be able to specify each other in order to communicate, which requires that the own IP address set on each PC be within the same network (here, the private IP address space 192.168.0.0/24) and not duplicated. An IP address is a number that uniquely identifies the party you communicate with, so if the same value is set on two machines in the same network, the addresses conflict and normal communication is not possible. In イ the addresses are 192.168.0.2 and 192.168.0.3, which meet the condition that the network part (192.168.0) is common while the host parts (2 and 3) differ. In other words, only イ has the combination of the same ESSID and different IP addresses within the same network, and that is the appropriate setting.

fields.before: The correct answer is ア, AI. The question asks for a mechanism that learns from things such as users’ past chat content and can infer an appropriate answer from the flow of the conversation. The technology that learns rules and patterns from data and infers (reasons out) an appropriate output for unknown input is exactly AI (Artificial Intelligence). Here, a chatbot (automated-response software) using AI learns from the accumulated dialogue data and generates answers that fit the context, thereby replacing operator-based human handling with automated handling. Because the keywords learning and inference connect directly to the core functions of AI, ア is the most appropriate.

fields.before: 正解はア。適切なものは a と b の二つだけである。まず a について、電子メールのウイルスは受信者のアドレス帳を利用して感染者本人が気付かないまま知人へ送信されたり、差出人アドレスを詐称する、いわゆるなりすましによって信用できる相手を装って送られてきたりする。つまり「誰から来たか」は「添付ファイルが安全か」の保証にはまったくならないので、信用できる人からのメールであっても添付ファイルのウイルスチェックを行うのは適切である。次に b について、音声や画像といった非実行ファイルは一見すると安全に思えるが、拡張子を偽装して実際には実行ファイルであるという手口があり、また画像や文書などのデータファイル自体に、それを開くアプリケーションの脆弱性を突く不正なデータが埋め込まれていて、開いた瞬間に不正なプログラムが動き出す例もある。したがってファイルの種類にかかわらずウイルスチェックを行うのは適切である。一方 c は明確に誤りで、プレビュー機能はメールを開く操作をしなくても本文を自動的に解釈して表示する機能であり、HTML メールに埋め込まれたスクリプトや不正なタグ、自動的に読み込まれる外部コンテンツが動作して、プレビューしただけで感染してしまう危険がある。安全性を確認するための手段どころか、それ自体が感染の契機になり得るので、不審なメールはプレビューも含めて開かず削除するのが正しい対処である。以上より適切なものは a と b だけであり、それだけをすべて挙げているアが正解となる。

fields.before: 正确答案是ア。恰当的只有 a 和 b 这两项。首先看 a，通过电子邮件传播的病毒会利用收件人的通讯录，在感染者本人毫无察觉的情况下发送给熟人，也会通过伪造发件人地址、即所谓的假冒（欺骗）伪装成可信任的对象发来。也就是说，“邮件来自谁”完全不能保证“附件是否安全”，因此即使是来自可信任的人的邮件，也要对附件进行病毒检查，这是恰当的。接着看 b，音频、图像等非可执行文件乍看之下似乎安全，但存在伪造扩展名、实际上却是可执行文件的手法；此外，图像或文档等数据文件本身也可能嵌入了针对打开它的应用程序漏洞的恶意数据，在打开的瞬间恶意程序就会运行。因此无论文件种类如何都要进行病毒检查，这是恰当的。另一方面，c 明显是错误的：预览功能是不执行打开邮件的操作也会自动解释并显示正文的功能，HTML 邮件中嵌入的脚本、恶意标签或自动加载的外部内容会因此运行，仅仅预览就有可能被感染。它非但不能作为确认安全性的手段，本身反而可能成为感染的契机，所以对可疑邮件的正确处理是连预览在内都不打开，直接删除。综上，恰当的只有 a 和 b，仅将它们全部列出的ア为正确答案。

fields.before: The correct answer is ア. Only a and b are appropriate. First, regarding a, an email virus may use the recipient’s address book to send itself to acquaintances without the infected person noticing, or it may arrive disguised as a trusted party through spoofing of the sender address. In other words, who the mail came from is no guarantee at all that the attachment is safe, so performing a virus check on the attachment even when the mail is from a person you trust is appropriate. Next, regarding b, non-executable files such as audio or images look safe at first glance, but there is a technique of faking the file extension so that the file is in fact an executable, and there are also cases where malicious data that exploits a vulnerability in the application opening the file is embedded in an image or document data file itself, so that a malicious program starts running the moment the file is opened. Therefore performing a virus check regardless of the type of file is appropriate. On the other hand, c is clearly wrong: the preview function automatically interprets and displays the body of a message without any action to open it, so a script or a malicious tag embedded in an HTML mail, or external content that is loaded automatically, can run and infect the machine merely from previewing. Far from being a way to confirm safety, it can itself become the trigger for an infection, so the correct handling of a suspicious email is to delete it without opening it, preview included. Hence only a and b are appropriate, and ア, which lists exactly those and nothing else, is the correct answer.
